title: Apple GPU M=1 two-output projection comparison
question: Does computing two adjacent M=1 projection outputs per SIMD group materially improve the 24-layer rotating QKV workload without materially regressing Q, KV, or hot QKV?
hypothesis: At M=1, two adjacent output rows of W reuse the same X values. Loading each X value once per lane and applying it to two FP32 accumulators may reduce input-load and scheduling overhead enough to improve the rotating-weight workload, while two independent warp reductions may increase register or reduction cost.

candidate.intended_production_dispatch: enqueue_linear_apple_gpu selects this path only when M=1 if and only if the frozen timing rule passes.
candidate.input_reuse: Each lane loads one X[0,k] value and applies it to two adjacent W rows.
unchanged: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output
candidate.scope_boundary: No vectorized loads, quantization, shared-weight tiling, combined-QKV kernel, general GEMM abstraction, or prefill optimization.

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo and the same frozen oracle fixtures used by the baseline
required_cases: M=1 with odd N to exercise the candidate tail
M>1 fallback through the public entrypoint
correctness.gate: Baseline, explicit candidate, and any promoted dispatch must match finite oracle output within the frozen tolerance before timing.

measurement_protocol.decisive_command: uv run --locked python benchmarks/run_linear.py --blocks 4 --experiment-id EXP-0005 --run-id EXP-0005-RUN-001 --variant-comparison --recorded --output-dir <absolute-external-path>/EXP-0005-RUN-001
measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and workload, candidate median divided by baseline median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain all ratios.

decision_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and candidate faster in at least three of four blocks.
decision_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and candidate slower in at least three of four blocks.
decision_rule.promote: Primary workload meets material improvement and no secondary workload meets material regression.
decision_rule.retain_baseline: Primary workload does not meet material improvement or any secondary workload meets material regression.
decision_rule.q_kv_crossover: Record opposite Q and KV effects, but add no N-based dispatch in this experiment.

generated_code_check.purpose: Verify the candidate lowers to two FP32 accumulation chains and two SIMD-group reductions without shared storage; not causal performance evidence.
expected: Two adjacent output rows are addressed per SIMD group.
Each input value feeds two weight multiply-accumulates.
Two warp reductions appear for a full output pair.
No threadgroup allocation or barrier is introduced.

profiling_rule: Profile the candidate only if ordinary paired timing finds a material primary effect. Compare the same Q and rotating workloads to the receipt-bound baseline attempts from EXP-0004.

production_rule.candidate_wins: Public Apple GPU projection dispatch selects the two-output kernel for M=1 and retains the one-output kernel for M>1.
production_rule.candidate_does_not_win: Public dispatch remains the one-output kernel for every M.
production_rule.always_retain: The explicit one-output and two-output measurement entrypoints remain available for reproducible comparison.

completion_conditions: Generated code matches the declared candidate structure.
All four recorded blocks pass environment, identity, order, and count gates.
The production choice follows the preregistered rule exactly.
Any qualifying profile is receipt-bound, or the mechanism remains unresolved.
nonclaims: No prefill, M>1 optimization, general GEMM, or combined-QKV result.
No end-to-end inference or model-level throughput result.
No hardware bandwidth or cache-reuse claim from source-level accounting.
No causal mechanism claim from timing alone.
